## TL;DR

Updated the public user guides for the Tailscale server listing, guarded review-verdict keep action, installed-update restart notice, and release retry behavior. The release engineering notes now explain the pushed-main recovery path, host-specific remote-validation detail, and the test that guards against version literals in tests. The docs site and landing builds passed; docs build regenerated and verified its three LLM text outputs and its changelog page data. The landing copy remains unchanged because the current copy makes no contradicted claim and does not list comparable CLI or restart-dialog details. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed, and the relevant redirect/LLM tests passed.

Task #1108 (idle-task auto-recovery) is still active, and #1109 (`repoos restart` for hand-started servers) is still in review. Neither was landed on main when this work began, so neither was added here.

## Work and rationale

I audited the task’s named user-facing changes against their implementation before editing. The `repoos servers --tailscale` documentation already had the correct option combinations and behavior: it discovers online Tailscale peers, falls back to configured hosts if the CLI is unavailable, reports unreachable hosts without losing local results, emits a host field in JSON, and does not allow `--prune` alongside Tailscale. I retained that description and added direct references to `src/commands/servers.ts` and its test.

The CLI guide did not document `repoos review keep <id>`. I added a command section describing its narrow purpose: keeping a completed verdict after a resolved close-out conflict only after RepoOS confirms the verdict and reviewed tree remain current. It continues the ordinary close-out pipeline and does not accept stale evidence or skip checks. The review guide now covers both this command and the error-card action, with implementation references to `DoneErrorCard.vue`, `src/commands/control-api.ts`, and `src/server/routes/tasks.ts`. It also identifies the server-side Land anyway reason and eligibility guard beside the existing explanation of the button.

The update guide already explained that an installed update can differ from the running server and that the user can restart immediately or when idle. It did not describe the new restart notice’s installed/running version display, the manual restart command’s copy button, or the release-notes scrolling area. I added those details and tied them to `src/ui-app/src/components/ReleaseUpdateNotification.vue`.

The public releases guide and `docs/releases.md` described retrying a committed bump, but omitted the behavior after an ambiguous branch-push result. The release code checks the remote branch tip: if it already points to the exact expected bump commit, the release proceeds to tagging. A later retry reuses the successful gate only when the exact commit and expected subject still match. I documented that behavior against `src/server/release.ts` and `src/ui-app/tests/release-status.test.ts`. I also documented that enabled remote release-validation details identify the failed host, and that transient infrastructure failure fails the release unless local fallback is enabled. Finally, the engineering notes now describe the `update-status.test.ts` guard that scans tests for literals equal to the current package version, preventing test fixtures from silently becoming stale on version bumps.

The generated changelog page data is loaded from the committed `release-history.json`; there was no release-history change in this docs-only task, so I did not hand-edit `CHANGELOG.md` or alter `user-docs/changelog.data.ts`. The successful VitePress build rendered the changelog page from that current source and regenerated `llms.txt`, `llms-essentials.txt`, and `llms-full.txt` under `user-docs/.vitepress/dist`. The build’s LLM and agent-guide checks passed. These outputs are build artifacts and are not tracked source files.

I read `landing/README.md` and the landing app source, including `landing/src/App.vue`. The current landing copy describes the broad task, worktree, check, and human-approval model; none of the audited details makes those statements inaccurate. There is no landing changelog surface that already lists comparable CLI commands, review recovery controls, or update-dialog behavior, so I left the landing copy untouched as requested. No marketing additions are proposed.

## Approaches tried

I first checked the task board and branch state. The board showed #1108 active and #1109 in review; neither had landed on main. I searched existing guides and implementation references to distinguish missing documentation from already-correct text, then made scoped edits only to the CLI, getting-started, review/close-out, deployments/releases, and release engineering guides.

The first docs build attempt could not find the VitePress executable, and the first landing build lacked `esbuild`. Both subprojects have their own lockfiles, so I installed their dependencies with `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in the respective project directories and reran the builds successfully. I then ran the required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. Its docs-only classification skipped general code checks and the configured full test step, so I ran the redirect, agent-file build, landing LLM text, and landing LLM cache test files explicitly with `bun run test`. The test run passed 43 tests across four requested files plus the wrapper’s boot-timing pass.

## Challenges and blockers

No implementation blocker remained. The VitePress build printed a warning that the sidebar points to `/getting-started#starting-a-new-project-as-an-agent`, for which it could not find a matching heading. The build still completed, the generated LLM index checks passed, and the warning is outside this feature-specific documentation audit, so I have not changed an unrelated sidebar link. The task’s conditional features #1108 and #1109 remain pending because their tasks had not landed on main at the start of this work.

## Key learnings

A docs-only RepoOS check can pass while skipping build and test steps by design; running the docs and landing builds directly plus the targeted redirect/LLM tests gave evidence for those explicit acceptance criteria. The docs changelog is derived from release history at build time, while the LLM files are VitePress build outputs; changing explanatory docs does not require manufacturing a release entry or editing the generated root changelog. For landing, the acceptance rule to update only an already-comparable surface prevents implementation details from being added as marketing copy without a product decision.
